questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Brazil?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brazil article.

questions.proof: Brazil's capital city is Brasília; its most populous city is São Paulo.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Brazil?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brazil article.

questions.proof: The country has the most Portuguese speakers in the world and is the only country in the Americas where Portuguese is an official language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is the world's fifth-largest country by area, behind _____, Canada, the United States, and China, with a total area of 8,514,877 square kilometers (3,287,612 sq mi).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “behind”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brazil article.

questions.proof: It is the world's fifth-largest country by area, behind Russia, Canada, the United States, and China, with a total area of 8,514,877 square kilometers (3,287,612 sq mi).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Soon, _____ colonized Brazil and created colonies all along the coastline.”

questions.proof: Soon, Portugal colonized Brazil and created colonies all along the coastline.
